scenes.visual: Title card: Neurotrophins switch on survival signals.

scenes.tts: Many developing neurons survive because a neurotrophin activates the right Trk receptor, said track. These receptors are kinases that switch on signals supporting survival and growth. That is how a neuron reads the factor its target supplies. The match matters: different groups of neurons depend on different factors and receptors. How does that survival signal start?

scenes.visual: Open with a target supplying neurotrophin to a developing neuron. Highlight its matching Trk receptor, then an intracellular green survival-and-growth signal. Show different factor-receptor matches on different neurons. Keep survival central; do not open with a death comparison.

scenes.tts: Mammals make four neurotrophins. N G F prefers Track A. B D N F and N T four prefer Track B. N T three prefers Track C, and activates Track A and Track B more weakly. Each factor is a dimer of two identical chains. It brings two Trk receptors together. Their kinase domains phosphorylate each other. The phosphorylated tyrosines start survival signals through Ras to E R K and P I three K to Akt.
scenes.narration: Mammals make four neurotrophins. NGF prefers TrkA. BDNF and NT-4 prefer TrkB. NT-3 prefers TrkC, and activates TrkA and TrkB more weakly. Each factor is a dimer of two identical chains. It brings two Trk receptors together. Their kinase domains phosphorylate each other. The phosphorylated tyrosines start survival signals through Ras to ERK and PI3K to Akt.

scenes.visual: Show the complete ligand map: NGF to TrkA; BDNF and NT-4 to TrkB; NT-3 to TrkC, with weaker arrows to TrkA and TrkB. Zoom into one factor dimer bringing two matching Trks together. Show reciprocal phosphorylation and green Ras–ERK and PI3K–Akt branches.

scenes.tts: Targets make a limited amount of survival factor. Neurons that fail to get enough die. Which factor a population depends on tracks the Trk receptor it makes and the factor its target makes. So the receptor map helps explain which developing neurons survive.

scenes.visual: Show a target supplying a limited pool of factor to developing neurons carrying matching Trks. Highlight sufficient factor reaching a surviving neuron, then insufficient support and loss of another. Connect the target factor and neuronal Trk to the population’s survival dependence.

scenes.tts: Mouse knockouts test those dependencies. Without N G F or Track A, mice lose sympathetic neurons and many small sensory neurons for pain and heat. Without B D N F, they lose sensory neurons for balance. Without N T three or Track C, they lose sensory neurons that report limb position. Different pairs give different patterns of loss.
scenes.narration: Mouse knockouts test those dependencies. Without NGF or TrkA, mice lose sympathetic neurons and many small sensory neurons for pain and heat. Without BDNF, they lose sensory neurons for balance. Without NT-3 or TrkC, they lose sensory neurons that report limb position. Different pairs give different patterns of loss.

scenes.visual: Compare control and knockout mice using three population diagrams: NGF/TrkA, sympathetic and pain/heat sensory neurons; BDNF, vestibular neurons; NT-3/TrkC, proprioceptive neurons. Show fewer neurons rather than implying every affected population is completely absent. End on the distinct patterns of loss.

scenes.tts: A shared receptor, p seventy five, binds all four neurotrophins. It has no kinase. It belongs to the tumor necrosis factor receptor family and carries a death domain. But its response depends on its partners. With Track A, it can raise N G F binding. With sortilin, it can carry a death signal.
scenes.narration: A shared receptor, p75, binds all four neurotrophins. It has no kinase. It belongs to the tumor necrosis factor receptor family and carries a death domain. But its response depends on its partners. With TrkA, it can raise NGF binding. With sortilin, it can carry a death signal.

scenes.visual: Show all four factors binding p75, with no kinase and an intracellular death domain. Then show its two contexts: cooperation with TrkA that raises NGF binding, and a p75–sortilin partnership capable of death signaling. Do not depict p75 as an automatic death switch or assert a settled physical TrkA–p75 architecture.

scenes.tts: Precursor processing adds another variable. N G F starts as a longer chain, pro N G F. Cells can secrete it uncut. In Hempstead's experiments, uncut pro N G F bound p seventy five tightly and triggered apoptosis of cultured sympathetic neurons. Later work showed that this death needs sortilin. Mature N G F supported survival through Track A. Another group found that uncut pro N G F could support survival too, more weakly. The outcome depends on processing and the balance of receptors.

scenes.visual: Closing application: merge the precursor explanation from s04_cut into this scene. Show a pro-domain on secreted proNGF, then the cultured sympathetic-neuron comparison: proNGF with p75 and sortilin can trigger apoptosis, while mature NGF activates TrkA survival. Add the alternative weaker survival result for uncut proNGF; do not imply uncut always kills. End with processing and receptor balance determining outcome.
End card: Matching neurotrophins and Trk receptors support neuronal survival.
